title: Read a versioned options struct
description:
A library's options struct has grown over three versions. Members were only ever added at the end:

```cpp
struct WorldOptions
{
    uint32_t size;        // set by the caller to sizeof the struct it was compiled with
    int32_t  width;       // version 1
    int32_t  height;      // version 1
    int32_t  gravity;     // version 2
    uint32_t seed;        // version 3
};
```

Write

```cpp
struct Settings { int32_t width; int32_t height; int32_t gravity; uint32_t seed; };

int32_t readOptions(const WorldOptions* options, Settings* out);
```

- A member is present when `options->size >= offsetof(WorldOptions, member) + sizeof(member)`.
- `width` and `height` are required: a null `options`, a null `out`, or a size too small for `height` is an error, code `1`, and `*out` is not written.
- Missing later members get defaults: `gravity` 10, `seed` 12345.
- A size **larger** than `sizeof(WorldOptions)` comes from a newer program: read what you know and ignore the rest.
- Return `0` on success.

Then write `uint32_t versionOfSize(uint32_t size)`: which version of the struct a size belongs to (1, 2 or 3; 3 for anything at least the version-3 size; 0 if smaller than version 1).

Because each member's position is fixed, a version-1 caller's struct is just the first bytes of the full struct. The tests build smaller structs by setting `size` to what a version-1 or version-2 caller would send.
hints: `offsetof(WorldOptions, gravity)` is 12 and `gravity` is 4 bytes, so a caller's struct contains `gravity` when its size is at least 16.
